Core plugins

Core plugins

A core plugin is the plugin form of a feature Ilium has today. Ilium ships and maintains all 30 of them, and each one has an id of the form ilium.core.<name>. Where a feature is native to the kernel, such as starting a process in a pane, the terminal emulator, the layout solver, the keymap or snapshots, the page says so and shows the plugin driving that kernel surface through contract version 0.1. See What a plugin is and Worlds and sides for the background.

[COR-050] Each of the 30 pages in the table MUST have a Complete manifest section, and the number of rows in this table MUST equal the number of core-plugin pages. The traceability of every Ilium feature to these plugins is in feature traceability, and the tests are in core parity requirements.

All core plugins

Plugin Id Side Scope
Tree ilium.core.tree both Groups, folders, moving, renaming, bookmarks and locks in the project tree.
Layout ilium.core.layout both Split views, mixed splits, focus, navigation and mouse resizing.
Terminal ilium.core.terminal both Pane processes, screen reads, scrollback, input, links and screen transfer.
Smart Copy ilium.core.smart-copy both Selection, the terminal right-click menu and Smart Copy.
Editor ilium.core.editor client Editor panes, highlighting, Markdown views and the file explorer.
Kanban ilium.core.kanban client Board panes, Markdown-backed boards and their settings.
Agent detection ilium.core.agent-detect both Agent identity, activity states, goals and custom signatures.
Agent toolbar ilium.core.agent-toolbar both Last-prompt banner, toolbar actions and per-agent frame facts.
Fleet ilium.core.fleet both Messaging many agents, ilium panes, broadcast and the local HTTP API.
Cost ilium.core.cost both Spend, quotas, session statistics and cost sorting.
Titles and organisation ilium.core.titles both Automatic titles, session naming and AI tree organisation.
Inference providers ilium.core.inference both AI providers, models, streaming and privacy controls.
Notifications ilium.core.notifications both Sounds, desktop notifications, toasts and attention marks.
Voice ilium.core.voice both Voice control, microphone capture and ilium voice say.
Scheduler ilium.core.scheduler both Scheduled input, the prompt queue and multi-stage input.
Text triggers ilium.core.text-triggers both Rules that watch terminal output and send text.
Progress ilium.core.progress both Progress monitors, ilium wait and the progress footer.
Chatroom ilium.core.chatroom both The shared CHATROOM.md, ilium chat and the message view.
Worktrees ilium.core.worktrees both Agents in Git worktrees and their branch status.
Sessions ilium.core.sessions server Snapshots, restore, recovery and detach and reattach.
Compaction ilium.core.compaction both Context compaction and the compaction optimiser.
Settings ilium.core.settings client The Settings screen, auto-save, onboarding and config files.
Keys and help ilium.core.keys-and-help client Prefix, keybindings, remapping, key reference and help topics.
Workspace search ilium.core.search both One panel to find agents, terminals and files.
Ambient look ilium.core.ambient client Shared colour, palette, dither and display for backgrounds.
Scenes ilium.core.scenes scene The animated background scenes themselves.
Recap ilium.core.recap both ilium recap: short and long factual recaps of panes.
Session conversion ilium.core.session-convert both Converting a transcript between Claude and Codex formats.
Agent setup ilium.core.agent-setup both Installing the Chatroom and Progress instruction blocks into agent config files.
Diagnostics ilium.core.diagnostics both File logging, log levels and the diagnostics report.

Which core plugins can be disabled

All 30 core plugins can be disabled except the essential set: ilium.core.tree, ilium.core.layout, ilium.core.settings and ilium.core.sessions. Safe mode keeps the essential set running (Safe mode and recovery). The Plugins screen shows a lock in the "Can be disabled" column for them. If the restart rule disables an essential plugin, the kernel fallback in Host architecture applies. [LIF-276]

  • [LIF-276] The Plugins screen MUST not offer a disable switch for the four essential plugins. Test: render the list and press Space on each.

How other plugins work with core plugins

Core plugins use only the public contract, so every way a third-party plugin can reach them is documented. There are five: observe (events and topics), drive (services and commands), extend (fill an extension point), offer (declare your own points) and replace (replaces). Every core page ends with an "Extension points" section that lists its points, services, topics and whether it can be replaced. Core extension points lists all of them. Extending core plugins explains when to use which, and Extension points is the reference.

Coverage

Every user-visible feature of Ilium maps to exactly one core plugin. Each plugin page lists the features it covers by their names in the user documentation, so you can start from a feature you know and find the plugin that implements it.

How the samples teach the ABI

The samples on these pages are short and focused. Together they illustrate the whole ABI: the matrix assigns each ABI area (API pages, widgets, settings row types, services, events and intents) one primary plugin, and that plugin's samples use it. Across the 30 pages there are 395 ABI pages linked from the "ABI used" sections, between 8 and 20 per plugin (counted by script over core-plugin-*.md). Each sample is given in Rust and in TypeScript, and every name in it appears on the linked ABI page. The calendar and api-gpu areas are unstable and the samples say so.

Renders and samples marked Illustrative are not test oracles. When a page differs from src/docs at the baseline commit, src/docs wins and the page is a defect. The exact values a test uses are in the "Behaviour contract" table of each page: a table with one row per rule, an id of the form <plugin>-B<nn>, the exact value or text, and the baseline source (src/docs/<file>.md#<anchor>, or the source file of the baseline crate when the user documentation is silent). The test oracle for a plugin is that table, checked against the baseline binary through the golden outputs in CLI compatibility.

Security

Replacement of core plugins follows [SEC-300] to [SEC-306] in Extension security.
